panels.rationale: Single-panel sagittal T1 MRI of the left knee from an article explicitly titled as describing skeletal manifestations in an adult Morquio syndrome (MPS IV) case. The in-text explicitly attributes genu valgus deformity, metaphyseal/epiphyseal widening, and severe bilateral knee articular cartilage involvement with osteoarthritic changes to Figures 7–9, establishing disease attribution to mucopolysaccharidosis_type_4. Genu valgum is a well-recognized classic skeletal manifestation of MPS IV and is present in the allowed vocabulary; the metaphyseal/epiphyseal widening and cartilage degeneration are explicitly described in-text but absent from the vocabulary, so they are listed as proposed findings. The image is a real human patient radiology image with no third-party restriction; subtype (Morquio A vs B) is not specified anywhere, so subtype is null. Skin tone is not assessable on MRI; no ethnicity is stated.

Thoracolumbar spine radiographs revealed anterior vertebral body wedging (Figure 1), platyspondyly, and increased interpedicular distance. Pelvic imaging showed an enlarged, oval‐shaped pelvic inlet accompanied by flared, rounded iliac wings. Chest radiography identified paddle‐shaped ribs (Figure 2).
